beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Riley's restless, dark circles under her eyes she didn't have last time.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I keep having this dream — back onstage with my old band, except something's always wrong, and I wake up before I find out what."

options.text: What does it feel like right before you wake up?
Dreams don't mean anything, ignore it.
That has nothing to do with your old band.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Dread, mostly. Like I'm about to make the same mistake twice."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: That dread might be worth trusting more than any plain explanation you'd give it.
Dread this specific means you should quit music altogether.
The dream is a coincidence, not a signal.

elaboration: Trust intuition and dreams over what's plainly stated — and a repeating cycle is worth noticing before it has the chance to repeat again.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "My old band actually called, wanting to talk. First time since the tour split. Is the dream about that?"

options.text: Maybe — what's hidden tends to surface in the dark, if you're actually willing to look at it.
It definitely means don't ever speak to them again.

elaboration: What's hidden becomes visible in the dark, if you're willing to look — and facing whatever that shadow side is turns out to be part of becoming whole.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Maybe I should actually pick up, instead of just dreaming around it."
